_why: @redrob-labs/ui deliberately ships no logo file: its Mark component takes src and darkSrc, so the
host supplies the artwork. There is no version to resolve, so these are pinned by sha256 and by
their path in the design system delivery.
What the hash is FOR. 10-logo.md: the artwork is 'Never redrawn, restretched, recolored or
otherwise modified', and lists recoloring, substituting the gradient and adding an effect (shadow,
outline, blur) under Incorrect usage. A brand file is the one asset here that a well-meaning edit
ruins silently: nudge the blue, flatten the gradient, re-export smaller, and every gate still
passes because no build reads a PNG's pixels. The hash is what fails.
Why two files. assets/Symbol/README.md gives each variant a ground: the gradient symbol belongs on
white and light grounds, solid-white on redrob-black and dark surfaces. One file cannot serve both,
and painting one through a CSS mask in a token colour is the recolor the spec forbids.
20-color.md closes the product spectrum at seven and states there is no eighth product colour.
10-logo.md's way out is that a new product ships as a feature of the product whose band it fits.
Recall's job is your own files and records on your own machine, which is Desk's band.
